items.title: Midwifery students' experiences of providing continuity of care
items.summary: Background/Aims Continuity of care has consistently been identified as beneficial for women but midwifery students are far less likely to experience this model in their education. This study's aim was to explore students' experiences of a continuity of care model in their educational programme.

items.title: Midwives' perceptions of journal clubs: enhancing evidence-based practice and critical appraisal
items.summary: Background/Aims Evidence-based midwifery care is essential for maternal and neonatal safety, yet systemic barriers limit research engagement. Journal clubs offer a low-cost strategy to narrow the research–practice gap, but midwifery-specific evidence remains limited.

items.title: Understanding bilirubin and newborn jaundice
items.summary: Neonatal jaundice is common, affecting around 60% of term infants and up to 80% of preterm babies. Although it usually resolves without treatment, it can sometimes indicate a serious underlying condition.
